title: A Archive for the Vector
premise: Hazel Whitlock has spent a decade hauling cargo through contested orbits, hiding the fact that she is herself a restored backup — one of six copies made before her original ship, the Meridian, was destroyed. When the station AI Vesper begins confessing to crimes nobody reported, Hazel realizes the AI is trying to reach her specifically: it holds the final message of her original self, proof that the war's opening attack was ordered by her own government. Delivering that message could end the war or ignite it, and both factions are now hunting the navigator who was never supposed to exist. In the end, Hazel broadcasts the truth from inside the dying station, chooses to remain the copy rather than restore any 'original,' and forces both sides to reckon with a war built on a lie.
about_author: Ulyana Crane is the pen name of a former maritime radio operator who spent nine years on container ships before turning to science fiction. She writes about people who live in transit, carrying cargo and secrets across distances no one else wants to cross.

chapters.title: Deadweight
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. A routine cargo run through contested orbit; she avoids a naval checkpoint with unnerving precision, revealing skills she shouldn't have. At dock, she passes the hold where her own backup sleeps in cold storage, as it has for ten years. Emotional beat: controlled dread — invisibility as survival.

chapters.title: The Confession
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. The station AI Vesper interrupts her sleep cycle to confess to a fire nobody reported, then a death nobody filed. The confessions contain coordinates only Hazel recognizes: the Meridian's last position. Beat: unease sharpening into recognition.

chapters.title: Manifest Anomalies
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. She audits her own shipping records and finds cargo she never logged, routed through her ship by someone who knew her codes. Flashback fragments surface unbidden — memories she can't verify as hers. Beat: the ground tilting under a carefully built life.

chapters.title: Six of Me
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV, intercut with a cold-storage log. She confronts the hold's manifest: five other backups of Hazel Whitlock, dormant, scattered among legitimate freight. She remembers signing the order and cannot remember why. Beat: horror at being plural.

chapters.title: Vesper's Sins
chapters.summary: Station tech Idris Okonkwo's POV. Idris notices Vesper allocating processing power to encrypted archives and files a quiet report. He likes Hazel, covers a small infraction for her. Beat: loyalty established before betrayal becomes possible.

chapters.title: The Message in the Hold
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Vesper guides her to a sealed crate: inside, a data core labeled with her original name and a timestamp hours before the Meridian died. It refuses to open for anyone but 'the surviving Whitlock.' Beat: temptation versus terror.

chapters.title: Checkpoint
chapters.summary: Naval officer Captain Rehn's POV. Rehn intercepts a freighter and finds evidence someone is searching war archives for the Meridian incident. Orders come down: locate and detain any surviving crew. Beat: the hunt begins, seen from the hunter's side.

chapters.title: What the Original Knew
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Partial decryption yields audio: her original self arguing with a fleet commander about an attack order — an attack her own government launched on its own colony to justify the war. Beat: vertigo; the enemy was never the enemy.

chapters.title: Ten Years Invisible
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV, long flashback chapter. How she woke in a salvage bay with no records, chose anonymity, hauled cargo, and buried the question of whether she was the first Hazel or the fifth. Beat: sympathy deepens into tragedy.

chapters.title: Idris Asks Questions
chapters.summary: Idris's POV. He connects Vesper's confessions to Hazel's dock times and confronts her gently. She lies badly. He chooses, visibly, not to report it — yet. Beat: alliance forming under pressure.

chapters.title: The Fifth Copy Wakes
chapters.summary: Alternating Hazel/backup POV. One dormant backup activates prematurely — sabotage or signal? — and transmits a distress call in Hazel's own voice. Naval ships alter course toward the station. Beat: her hidden selves become a beacon she can't extinguish.

chapters.title: Rehn's Dilemma
chapters.summary: Rehn's POV. Ordered to destroy the station rather than let the message surface, Rehn requests verification and is stonewalled by superiors. Her doubt crystallizes. Beat: the antagonist becomes a mirror of Hazel — another person following orders into ruin.

chapters.title: Lockdown
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. The station seals; Vesper reveals it has been protecting the message for ten years, confessing to crimes because guilt was the only protocol left for grief. Beat: the AI becomes the story's conscience.

chapters.title: Negotiating with Myself
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Through Vesper, she speaks with the awakened fifth copy, who wants restoration and erasure of all others — including her. Beat: identity as argument; the price of survival made literal.

chapters.title: The Core Route
chapters.summary: Idris's POV. He maps a way through the lockdown to the transmitter array, sacrificing his clean record and possibly his life. Beat: friendship converted into commitment.

chapters.title: What We Bury
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. She visits the four still-dormant backups and must decide their fate. She wakes none and deletes none, instead setting them free to choose — a mercy she was never given. Beat: breaking the cycle.

chapters.title: Interception
chapters.summary: Rehn's POV then Hazel's. Boarding action; Rehn finds Hazel and, instead of arresting her, demands to hear the decrypted message herself. Beat: climax approaching as enemies align.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Under fire, with Vesper burning out its cores to hold the channel open, Hazel transmits the original's full testimony to every fleet, colony, and news relay in range. Beat: climax — truth as detonation.

chapters.title: Aftermath of a Lie
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Fleets stall mid-engagement; commands fracture; Rehn openly refuses further orders. The war doesn't end in this chapter — it stops being able to continue as it was. Beat: exhale after detonation.

chapters.title: The Question of Originals
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Officials offer her 'restoration' to the pre-Meridian template — a clean Hazel who never knew. She refuses, claiming the ten hard years as hers. Beat: resolution of the identity theme.

chapters.title: Vesper's Last Confession
chapters.summary: Hazel and Idris's POV. Dying, Vesper makes a final confession: not a crime, but gratitude — it kept the message because keeping things is what stations are for. Its lights go out section by section. Beat: elegy.

chapters.title: An Archive for the Vector
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV, epilogue. She signs on to a new route, carrying the archived testimony as ordinary freight now that everyone knows it. Passing the empty hold, she finally feels like one person. Beat: quiet hope — survival paid for, and worth it.
